definitions.fermentable_carbohydrates: Carbohydrates or carbohydrate mixtures as consumed in foods or beverages that lower plaque pH below 5.7, as determined in vivo or in situ by plaque pH telemetry tests, by bacterial fermentation during and up to 30 minutes after consumption.
definitions.non_fermentable_carbohydrates: Carbohydrates or carbohydrate mixtures as consumed in foods or beverages that do not lower plaque pH, as determined in vivo or in situ by plaque pH telemetry tests, below a conservative value of 5.7 by bacterial fermentation during and up to 30 minutes after consumption.

conditions.reference_regulation: Energy and protein requirements, WHO/FAO/UNU Meeting, WHO Technical Report Series 724
conditions.info: In order to bear the claim, a food should comply with the following requirements: 1. Energy content shall not be less than 200 kcal (840 kJ) and shall not exceed 250 kcal (1046 KJ) per meal. 2. Fat content and composition: Energy derived from fat shall not exceed 30% of total available energy. Linoleic acid (in the form of glycerides) shall not be less than 1 g. 3. Protein content and composition: The protein contained in the food shall provide not less than 25% and not more than 50% of the total energy content. The chemical index of protein shall be equal to that set by the WHO in ‘Energy and protein requirements’ (1985, WHO Technical Report Series 724). If the chemical index is lower than 100% of the reference protein, the minimum protein levels shall be correspondingly increased. In any case, the chemical index of the protein shall at least be equal to 80% of that of the reference protein. 4. Vitamins and minerals: The food shall provide at least 30% of the nutrient reference values per meal as laid down in Annex XIII to Regulation (EU) No 1169/2011, except for fluoride, chromium, chloride, and molybdenum. The amount of sodium per meal shall be at least 172.5 mg, and potassium at least 500 mg. Information shall be provided to the consumer on the importance of maintaining an adequate daily fluid intake and that the products are useful only as part of an energy-restricted diet.
